topic: What are the trade-offs in using additive manufacturing for CTS array fabrication versus traditional methods in terms of deployment cost and scalability?
consensus_response: Additive manufacturing (AM) for CTS array fabrication offers design freedom, compactness, and reduced material and assembly costs. However, it may compromise on thermal conductivity, introducing higher surface roughness and reduced reliability. The complexity of AM-produced corrugations can also introduce additional fabrication costs. Traditional methods, such as milling and electroerosion, ensure precise thickness control, minimizing thermal losses and enhancing component lifespan. The trade-offs between AM and traditional methods depend on the specific requirements of the CTS array and the cost and availability of the necessary equipment and materials.
